parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Method 1: set $y=\frac2{ax-3}+\frac12$ and rearrange to $\left(y-\frac12\right)(ax-3)=2$, or $ax-3=\frac2{y-\frac12}$ — *M1 OE; condone sign errors only. Make $ax$ the subject: $ax=\frac4{2y-1}+3$ — DM1; condone sign errors only. $g^{-1}(x)=\frac4{a(2x-1)}+\frac3a$, or $\frac2{a(x-\frac12)}+\frac3a$, equivalently $\frac1a\left(3+\frac4{2x-1}\right)$ — A1 OE; $x$ and $y$ may be interchanged from the start. Clearly replace $a$ with 6 in $g^{-1}$ and, if necessary, simplify to arrive at exactly the same expression as $g(x)$ — A1, dependent on obtaining the correct inverse. Alternative method: write $y=\frac{ax+1}{2(ax-3)}$ and rearrange to $2y(ax-3)=ax+1$ — *M1 OE; condone sign errors only. Make $ax(2y-1)$ the subject: $ax(2y-1)=6y+1$ — DM1; condone sign errors only. $g^{-1}(x)=\frac{3x+\frac12}{a(x-\frac12)}$, or $\frac{6x+1}{a(2x-1)}$ — A1 OE; $x$ and $y$ may be interchanged from the start. Clearly replace $a$ with 6 and simplify to exactly $g(x)$ — A1, dependent on obtaining the correct inverse. Total 4.
